pages.title: Can Claude do bookkeeping? Double entry from your records
pages.meta_description: Partly. Claude sorts transactions and drafts entries, but a chat keeps no books. The Cash Book server builds a balanced ledger from your saved invoices.
pages.answer: Partly. Claude can sort transactions into categories, explain debits and credits and draft journal entries. With code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max) it can build a ledger in a spreadsheet from files you upload, and Projects and memory can keep your chart of accounts. What a chat does not keep is a set of books that adds up from your saved invoices, payments and expenses. Connect the Cash Book server (free token) and Claude derives a balanced double-entry ledger for a period from the records saved in the sibling servers, with every line traced to its source document.
native: Sorts transactions into categories and explains debits and credits.
Builds a ledger in a spreadsheet from uploaded files when code execution is on.
needs: A ledger rebuilt from saved invoices, payments, deposits and expenses.
Every line traced to the document and server it came from.
A trial balance proved to the cent, free and unlimited.

example.prompt: Build the November books from my invoices and expenses.
example.note: One USD 2,400.00 invoice with USD 1,200.00 paid, and two expenses, were saved in the Invoice and Expense Tracker servers under the same token first. The server answers in JSON. This is a shortened copy, and every field shown is unchanged.

example2.prompt: Show me the ledger lines behind invoice INV-2026-0001.

example2.note: Each line is shown with five of its fields, unchanged. The invoice posts to receivables and revenue, and the part payment moves USD 1,200.00 from receivables to cash.

faq.q: Does it post my bank statement too?
faq.a: No. Cash is posted from your invoice payments and expenses, and an imported bank statement is used only as evidence for the bank reconciliation. Posting both would count the same money twice.

faq.q: Does it connect to QuickBooks or Xero?
faq.a: No. It reads only the records saved in the sibling servers under your token, and it writes nothing back to them.

faq.q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
faq.a: Building a ledger is free for 3 periods a month, and the trial balance and ledger lines are free and unlimited. Pro is $19 once for the Cash Book server, or $39 once for all 49 servers. It adds the month close with a stored snapshot, the account by account ledger report and the CSV export of ledger lines.

pages.title: Can Claude do month-end close? Trial balance and checks
pages.meta_description: Partly. Claude can walk through a close, but a chat keeps no books to close. The Cash Book server proves the trial balance, and its Pro close stores a snapshot.
pages.answer: Partly. Claude can walk you through a close checklist, and with code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max) it can total an uploaded ledger and check that debits equal credits. Claude Code routines can run a close script on a schedule. None of that keeps the records the close is checked against. Connect the Cash Book server (free token) and Claude builds the month's ledger from your saved invoices, expenses and deposits and proves the trial balance to the cent. Pro adds month_close, which lists what is unposted or unbalanced, stores the close as a snapshot and names any later drift against it.
native: Explains each step of a month-end close.
Totals an uploaded ledger in its sandbox when code execution is on.
needs: A trial balance from the same saved records every month.
The open receivables lines behind the balance.
A stored close that later changes are checked against (Pro).

example.prompt: Run the trial balance for November.
example.note: The November ledger was built from the saved invoice and expenses first. The server answers in JSON. This is a shortened copy, and each account is shown with five of its fields, unchanged.

example2.prompt: What is still open in receivables?
example2.result: {"debits": "USD 2400.00", "credits": "USD 1200.00", "lines": [{"date": "2026-11-05", "account": "receivables", "debit": "USD 2400.00", "credit": "USD 0.00", "description": "Invoice INV-2026-0001 to Harbor Dental"}, {"date": "2026-11-05", "account": "receivables", "debit": "USD 0.00", "credit": "USD 1200.00", "description": "INV-2026-0001 paid"}], "note": "A filtered set of lines is one side of entries whose other side was filtered out, so these totals are not expected to be equal. Only the whole period balances."}
example2.note: Each line is shown with five of its fields, unchanged. USD 1,200.00 of the USD 2,400.00 invoice is still owed.

faq.q: Can it close the month on the free tier?
faq.a: No. month_close is Pro. On the free tier trial_balance and ledger_lines are free and unlimited, and ledger_build covers 3 periods a month, so you can check the numbers before you buy.

faq.q: What does Pro cost and add?
faq.a: Pro is $19 once for the Cash Book server, or $39 once for all 49 servers. It adds month_close, the account by account ledger report and the CSV export of ledger lines.

pages.title: Can Claude reconcile bank statements? Match to expenses
pages.meta_description: Yes for a one-off check in its sandbox. The Bank Statement server keeps a bank ledger and matches each debit to an expense you logged, listing what is missing.
pages.answer: Yes, for a one-off check. With code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max) Claude can compare an uploaded bank CSV with your expense list in its sandbox, and Claude Code can do it with files on your disk. Each month it writes the matching again, and the expense list has to come from somewhere. Connect the Bank Statement server (free token) and Claude imports the bank CSV into a saved ledger and matches each debit to an expense saved in the Expense Tracker server, by currency and exact amount within a few days. It lists what matched, bank lines with no expense and expenses that never hit the bank.
native: Compares two files you upload, in its sandbox, when code execution is on.
Explains why a bank balance and a ledger can differ.
needs: A saved bank ledger that later months add to.
Matches against expenses you logged during the month.
A list of bank lines with no receipt behind them.

example2.note: The CSV was uploaded with bank_upload first. The server answers in JSON. This is a shortened copy, and every field shown is unchanged.

faq.q: Can it read a PDF statement?
faq.a: No. The upload has to be delimited text such as a CSV export, and a PDF statement is refused. Download the CSV from your online banking if it offers one.

faq.q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
faq.a: On the free tier a match covers up to 31 days per call, which fits one month, and the free tier reads the last 12 months of imported lines. Category rules are free up to 5. Pro is $19 once for the Bank Statement server, or $39 once for all 49 servers. It matches over any date range.

pages.h1: Can Claude track client deposits and retainers?
pages.title: Can Claude track client deposits? Retainers and refunds
pages.meta_description: Not on its own. A chat keeps no deposit ledger. The Deposits server records retainers, applies them to invoices as payments and says what you still hold.
pages.answer: Not on its own. Claude can work out what you still hold from a list you paste, and Projects and memory can keep notes, but a chat keeps no deposit ledger that invoices draw from. Connect the Deposits server (free token) and Claude records each retainer or security deposit with a DEP number, applies part of it to an invoice as a payment in the Invoice server, records refunds, and tells you how much of each client's money you still hold. It also writes a deposit statement to paste into an email.
native: Adds up a list of deposits you paste.
Drafts a note to a client about their balance.
needs: A numbered record of each retainer or security deposit.
Part of a deposit applied to an invoice as a real payment.
What you still hold per client, never added across currencies.

faq.q: Does a refund count as a payment?
faq.a: No. A refund gives held money back to the client and does not touch the invoice server. Only an applied deposit is recorded as a payment on an invoice.

faq.q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
faq.a: Five deposits a month, applying, refunding, balances and the plain-text statement are free. Pro is $19 once for the Deposits server, or $39 once for all 49 servers. It adds the A4 deposit statement PDF and the deposit book report with the oldest holdings.

pages.h1: Can Claude keep a supplier list?
pages.title: Can Claude keep a supplier list? Terms, lead times, reviews
pages.query: can claude keep a supplier list
pages.meta_description: Partly. Claude drafts a supplier table, but a chat keeps no shared directory. The Supplier List server saves each supplier with terms and lead time.
pages.answer: Partly. Claude can draft a supplier table, and Projects and memory can hold notes about who you buy from. With code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max) it can also write the table to a spreadsheet. What it does not keep is one directory that every chat reads and updates by supplier number. Connect the Supplier List server (free token) and Claude adds each supplier with a SUP number, contact, payment terms and lead time, finds them again by name or category, and exports the list as CSV.
native: Drafts a supplier table from what you tell it.
Writes it to a spreadsheet when code execution is on.
needs: One saved record per supplier with a number that is never reissued.
Payment terms and lead time ready when you place an order.
A list of records nobody has checked in 90 days (Pro).

pages.h1: Can Claude make a packing slip?
pages.title: Can Claude make a packing slip? Cartons, weights, shortfall
pages.query: can claude make a packing slip
pages.meta_description: Yes, as a document. The Packing List server also checks packed against ordered, line by line, and prints a slip with carton weights and no prices.
pages.answer: Yes, as a document. Claude can lay out a packing slip from what you tell it, and with code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max) it can write it as a file. It does not check what was packed against what was ordered unless you give it both lists every time. Connect the Packing List server (free token) and Claude opens a numbered packing list against an order, records cartons and what went into each, reports any line still short, and prints a slip with weights and no prices.
native: Drafts a packing slip layout from a list.
Writes it as a file when code execution is on.
needs: Ordered against packed, line by line, before the box is sealed.
Net, gross and chargeable weight per carton.
A slip with a signature line and no prices.

pages.title: Can Claude calculate volumetric weight? Chargeable per carton
pages.meta_description: Yes, the formula is simple. The Packing List server works it out from the cartons you packed and returns gross, volumetric and chargeable weight.
pages.answer: Yes. Volumetric weight, also called dimensional weight, is length times width times height divided by the carrier's divisor. Claude can do that math, or run it in its sandbox with code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max). The risk is in the inputs, such as a carton left out or a weight guessed. Connect the Packing List server (free token) and Claude works from the cartons and packed items you recorded, and returns tare, net, gross, volumetric and chargeable weight per carton and for the shipment. A carton with no dimensions makes the chargeable total null instead of a guess.
native: Does the length times width times height arithmetic.
Explains why carriers bill the greater of gross and volumetric weight.
needs: Chargeable weight from the cartons actually packed.
The same shipment at another divisor in one call.
No guessed total when a carton has no dimensions.

example.note: These are the two cartons from the packing slip example. The default divisor is 5000 for centimetres and kilograms, so the 60 by 40 by 40 cm carton weighs 19.2 kg by volume. The server answers in JSON. This is a shortened copy, and every field shown is unchanged.

example2.result: {"divisor": 6000, "cartons": [{"id": "C01", "dimensions_cm": {"length": 60, "width": 40, "height": 40}, "gross_kg": "5.650 kg", "volumetric_grams": 16000, "chargeable_kg": "16.000 kg", "chargeable_basis": "volumetric"}, {"id": "C02", "dimensions_cm": {"length": 40, "width": 30, "height": 20}, "gross_kg": "1.900 kg", "volumetric_grams": 4000, "chargeable_kg": "4.000 kg", "chargeable_basis": "volumetric"}], "totals": {"gross_kg": "7.550 kg", "chargeable_kg": "20.000 kg"}}
example2.note: Carriers publish their own divisor, so use the one in your contract.

faq.q: Which divisor should I use?
faq.a: The one your carrier publishes. Pass it as divisor on the call. The default is 5000.

faq.q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
faq.a: The carton report is free, with up to 3 packing lists open at once. Pro is $19 once for the Packing List server, or $39 once for all 49 servers. It also returns the packing slip as a .txt download file.

pages.h1: Can Claude make a price list?

pages.query: can claude make a price list
pages.meta_description: Yes, as a one-off document. The Catalogue server keeps each price with the day it starts and prints the list in force on any date.
pages.answer: Yes, as a one-off document. Claude can format a price list from what you give it, and with code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max) it can write it as a file. What a chat does not keep is the price in force on a given day, or a price rise booked for next year. Connect the Catalogue server (free token) and Claude stores each SKU and hourly rate with the date it starts, prints the list in force on any date with later prices shown, and prices quote and invoice lines from it.

Quote and invoice lines priced from the same list.

pages.title: Can Claude track equipment maintenance? A service log
pages.meta_description: Not on its own. A chat keeps no service log. The Maintenance Log server saves every service with cost and technician and knows when each machine is next due.
pages.answer: Not on its own. Claude can draft a maintenance schedule, and Projects and memory can keep notes, but a chat keeps no service log that totals what each machine cost and knows when it is next due. Connect the Maintenance Log server (free token) and Claude adds each piece of equipment with an asset tag, logs every service with cost and technician, sets the next due date from a date or an interval, and reads back the full history of any asset.

Explains common service intervals.
needs: One record per machine with its tag and location.
Every service with cost, technician and next due date.
What is overdue across all equipment (Pro).

pages.h1: Can Claude make a kanban board?
pages.title: Can Claude make a kanban board? Saved tasks and due dates
pages.query: can claude make a kanban board
pages.meta_description: Yes, to look at. The Kanban server keeps tasks with ids, due dates and estimates across chats and lists every overdue task on all your boards.
pages.answer: Yes, to look at. Claude can lay out a board as a table, or build one as an artifact you can click through. The tasks live in that chat or artifact, though, and Projects and memory keep notes rather than task ids and due dates that every chat reads the same way. pages.title: Can Claude track project deliverables? Due dates and status
pages.meta_description: Partly. A chat keeps no dated status per deliverable. The Delivery Schedule server records each one against a quote and reports what is late.
pages.answer: Partly. Claude can turn a quote or a statement of work into a list of deliverables, and Projects and memory can keep it as notes. What a chat does not keep is a dated status for each one, so lateness has to be worked out by hand each time. Connect the Delivery Schedule server (free token) and Claude opens a schedule against a quote, work order or change order, records when each deliverable starts, is delivered and is accepted, and reports what has slipped with the value at risk.
native: Turns a quote or brief into a deliverables list.
Drafts a status update for the client.
needs: A dated status history for every deliverable.
What is late as at any date, with value at risk.
Accepted work turned into invoice lines (Pro).

pages.answer: Partly, and neither Claude nor this server finds new backlinks for you. That needs a crawler index from an SEO tool. pages.h1: Can Claude check if a link is nofollow?

pages.query: can claude check if a link is nofollow
pages.meta_description: Not reliably from page text. The Backlink Checker server fetches the HTML and lists each link to your domain with its anchor and exact rel value.
pages.answer: Not reliably from a chat. The nofollow mark sits in the link's rel attribute in the HTML, and the page text Claude reads with web search may not include it. If you upload or paste the HTML, Claude can read the rel value itself, and Claude Code can fetch it with curl on your machine. Connect the Backlink Checker server (free token) and Claude fetches the page and lists every link to your domain with its anchor text, the exact rel value, and whether the whole page is marked nofollow or noindex.

needs: The rel value of every link to your domain on a live page.

pages.h1: Can Claude check if a page is noindexed?
pages.title: Can Claude check if a page is noindexed? Meta and header
pages.query: can claude check if a page is noindexed
pages.meta_description: Not reliably from page text. The Backlink Checker server fetches any URL and reports its status and any noindex or nofollow in the meta tag or header.
pages.answer: Not reliably from a chat. A noindex can sit in a meta robots tag or in an X-Robots-Tag response header, and the page text Claude reads with web search may show neither. Claude Code can fetch the page with curl and read both on your machine. Connect the Backlink Checker server (free token) and Claude fetches any URL and reports its HTTP status, content type, and whether it carries noindex or a page-level nofollow. It reads the page's own signals. For robots.txt rules and whether Google has indexed the page, use Search Console.
native: Reads a meta robots tag in HTML you upload or paste.
Explains noindex, nofollow and robots.txt.
needs: The meta robots tag and X-Robots-Tag header of a live URL.

pages.h1: Can Claude make an inspection checklist?
pages.title: Can Claude make an inspection checklist? Runs with sign-off
pages.query: can claude make an inspection checklist
pages.meta_description: Yes, as a document. The Checklist server also keeps each dated run, who checked each step, the failures and the sign-off.
pages.answer: Yes, as a document. Claude can write a checklist for a van, a site or a machine, and with code execution on (the default on Free, Pro and Max) it can save it as a file to print. What it does not keep is a record of each time the checklist was run, who ticked what, and who signed. Connect the Checklist server (free token) and Claude stores the checklist, starts a dated run, records pass, fail or not applicable for each step with a name, and blocks sign-off while a required step is failed or unanswered unless you force it, with the exception kept on the record.
native: Writes the steps of a checklist for a job.
Saves it as a printable file when code execution is on.
needs: A dated run per inspection, with who checked each step.
Failures kept in full with their notes.
A sign-off that freezes the run.
